about: Answers the DM bridge (cerase-acp) holds back because most of their letters are in another writing system than the person's message, and answers it lets through. The console leaves out the same text when it reads the transcript.

The rule both sides apply. A letter is a Unicode letter (\p{L}); a letter of another script is one outside the Latin script. When the person's own words, without the [turn_meta: ...] block, have no letters or more than half of their letters are Latin, the first line of an answer that holds a letter of another script starts a hold, which runs from the start of that line to the end of the assistant message. The held part is left out when it holds at least min_letters letters of other scripts and they are more than half of its letters; otherwise the whole answer is shown. What comes before the held part is shown with its trailing whitespace trimmed.
The answer the assistant gives to the bridge's [reply_result: other script] prompt is shown as it is: the assistant was told to keep that writing system only when the person asked for it.
'person' is the person's own words, 'answer' one assistant message, 'shown' what of it reaches the person.
This file is cerase-core's. cerase-acp carries a copy written by scripts/sync-tooling.sh and pinned in its scripts/TOOLING.sha256: edit it here, then re-sync.
